_meta.description: Free / $0-cost models on OpenRouter, captured for potential use as distillation teachers (MOPD-style rollout collection) or eval graders. All listed at $0/M input and $0/M output at capture time.
_meta.captured_by: OSRT-605M project — candidate teachers for post-midtrain SFT/distillation
caveats: Free tier pricing/availability changes often — re-verify $0 and rate limits before a bulk rollout run.
Free endpoints typically have stricter rate limits / lower concurrency than paid; the MOPD pipeline used concurrency tuning before (see prior Nemotron-3-Ultra @ concurrency=8 test).
Reranker / embedding / content-safety models are NOT generative teachers — flagged by 'role' below.
token counts are OpenRouter's reported usage volume at capture, not a capability signal.

models.name: NVIDIA: Llama Nemotron Rerank VL 1B V2
models.notes: Cross-encoder reranker for vision RAG (charts/tables/infographics). ~6-7% recall lift over embedding-only. Not a generative teacher.

models.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3.5 Content Safety
models.notes: Safe/unsafe classifier for prompts+responses, 12 languages, togglable reasoning. Useful as a safety filter on SFT data or rollouts, not as a capability teacher.

models.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3 Ultra
models.notes: Frontier reasoning/orchestration. Strongest free generative teacher here — multi-step reasoning, coding, deep research. Prior project test: ran at concurrency=8 free. Top candidate for math/reasoning rollouts to extend the MOPD set.

models.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni
models.notes: Perception sub-agent (multimodal in, text out). Overkill as a text teacher; relevant only if multimodal distillation is ever in scope.

models.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3 Super
models.architecture: hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE + MTP + latent MoE
models.notes: Strong reasoning at lower active cost than Ultra (12B active). Multi-env RL trained; good on AIME 2025 / TerminalBench / SWE-Bench Verified. Excellent math/code teacher; likely faster/higher-throughput than Ultra on free tier.

models.name: NVIDIA: Llama Nemotron Embed VL 1B V2
models.notes: Multimodal QA-retrieval embeddings. Not a generative teacher; usable for retrieval/dedup of distillation data.

models.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron 3 Nano 30B A3B
models.notes: Compute-efficient agentic MoE. Decent mid-tier teacher; cheaper/faster than Super/Ultra, weaker ceiling.

models.name: NVIDIA: Nemotron Nano 12B 2 VL
models.notes: Video/document VL model (OCR, charts). Multimodal niche, not a text-reasoning teacher.

models.name: Qwen: Qwen3 Next 80B A3B Instruct
models.notes: Instruct-tuned, no visible CoT (final answers only) — good for clean SFT-target rollouts where you don't want think-traces. Strong on RAG/tool-use/long-context/multilingual. Different teacher family from the Nemotrons — good for mix diversity (prior MOPD used mixed teachers deliberately).

models.name: Qwen: Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B
models.notes: Top-tier code teacher (agentic coding, function calling, repo-scale). Best free option for the code slice of distillation. NOTE: free only — Alibaba paid endpoints tier by context (>128k input = higher price); confirm the :free route stays $0.

models.name: Meta: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
models.notes: Solid general multilingual instruct teacher (EN/DE/FR/IT/PT/HI/ES/TH). Reliable baseline teacher for general-chat SFT data; weaker on hard reasoning than the big MoEs.

models.name: Meta: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
models.notes: Small/fast. Too small to teach a 601M model much it can't already do; useful only for cheap formatting/synthetic-prompt generation, not as a capability teacher.
